summary: Gallatin County, MT ground-level lookout (log cabin c.1914, L-4 cab 1931), listed abandoned and gone; a 1934 Forest Service rental cabin on the same trail is not tied to it.

facts.design: Log cabin (c.1914), later an L-4 cab (1931)
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says abandoned and gone, with no dates; the FFLA Montana list marks it gone

access.note: No source describes access to the old lookout site. A separate Forest Service rental, Windy Pass Cabin, is open June 16 to October 14 and has no motorized access

visit.trail_note: Windy Pass Cabin, the 1934 rental, is a 2.5-mile hike or horseback ride up the Windy Pass Trail with a 1,300 ft climb. No source describes a route to the old lookout site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 9,160 feet for the lookout. The Forest Service and Wild Montana give about 8,900 feet for the 1934 rental cabin. No source links the two sites, so the story treats them as separate.
The 1934 rental cabin shares the name Windy Pass and the trail. Its build date does not fit the c.1914 and 1931 lookout dates, and no source ties the two together, so the story keeps them apart.

notes_for_editor: The old lookout's status rests on firelookout.com and the FFLA list, and neither gives dates for abandonment or removal. The 1934 Windy Pass Cabin is a live Forest Service rental and may confuse readers; the story says no source ties it to the lookout. The brief's ground-level kind is confirmed by the FFLA list. No staffing or fire records found. Access to the old site is unknown.
